Subject: QBR sprintflow: consolidated runway + account-by-account action rotations

Team —

QBR next week is locked. For the leadership readout I want a tight rollup: a single consolidated forecast (owner-level rollup + net new motions) and cleaned account one-pagers for each top-30 runway accounts. Key asks (priority order):

1) Fill the attached QBR_runway_template_v2.xlsx for your owned accounts (status, forecast, main blocker, next milestone, variance to prior forecast).
2) For any account > $400k ARR potential, add a 1-paragraph risk note and the mitigation owner.
3) Add HubSpot deal ids in the template (column: HS id) — this helps tie to finance exports.
4) Collate any legal/procurement obstacles (procurement contacts, redline status) as a separate sheet.

Delivery cadence: preliminary consolidated forecast by EOD Wednesday (May 5). Final deck material by Friday COB.

I want concise bullets in the email thread — no long attachments until we need them. If you need me to step into a call with Acme or Brightbyte to unblock procurement, flag it here and cc the right exec.

Thanks —
Markus
Markus Klein
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Markus —

Got it. I ran a quick consolidation against the latest bookings extracts and put a first-pass CSV up (attached). High-level notes:

- Total top-30 runway: $12.1M ARR equivalent; ~38% concentrated in top 5 accounts.
- Acme Corp currently shows at $1.9M open potential (HS-23124) but procurement hold may push commit Q out of plan.
- Brightbyte is trending late-stage but needs an SSO scoping call; pipeline shows as commit in May but probability should be adjusted from 70% -> 45% pending engineering review.

I attached forecast_consolidation_v1.csv for owners to review. I also inserted a 'variance' column where owners had updated forecasts in the last 7 days.

Questions for the thread: do we want to apply the conservative gating (move anything with active procurement redline to 'at risk') or keep the optimistic commit numbers for the leadership rollup? My recommendation: mark as 'at risk' and present both optimistic/conservative totals in the deck.

-Karthik
